notes: ID normalization was a non-issue in practice: all 1272 raw node IDs across the 24 batch files already matched the assembled graph 1:1 (no dupes, no collisions), so the 'Fixed' section's implied ID-rewriting had nothing to actually change here.
No nodes were missing an 'id' field, and complexity values were already all valid (simple/moderate/complex) — no remapping needed.

One unusual but well-formed node type found: 'schema' (57 nodes, all supabase/migrations/*.sql files). IDs correctly use the 'file:' prefix despite the type; this looks like an intentional semantic subtype for DDL/migration files rather than an error, so it was left as-is.

Investigated all 43 dangling edges from the raw batch union (2419 raw -> 2383 kept by merge script). The vast majority (~25) point to plain exported constants/types (e.g. CONTRACT_TYPES, PERSONA_TEMPLATES, ATHENA_MODELS, buttonVariants) that their own batch legitimately chose not to model as separate nodes -- confirmed by reading the source files. These match the merge script's own characterization of 'expected LLM significance-filtering imprecision' and were left dropped.

Recovered 3 genuine omissions where a batch modeled some but not all exports of a file it directly analyzed: getSettings in src/lib/settings.ts (batch-11 only modeled sibling getProfile), getAuthUser in src/lib/supabase/server.ts (batch-7-part-2 only modeled sibling createClient), and the proxy() function in src/proxy.ts (batch-20 modeled the file but no function at all). All three are heavily called (getSettings/getAuthUser from 8 dashboard/API route files; proxy is the app's Next.js middleware entry point) -- verified against actual source. Added the 3 nodes plus the 16 'calls'/'contains' edges that referenced them.

Also fixed 2 edges with a wrong type-prefix in their target (class:...OliveVines and class:...WaitlistForm) -- both are actually modeled as type 'function', not 'class'. Retargeted and re-added these 'related' CSS-co-location edges pointing to the correctly-prefixed function IDs.

Cross-batch import-map check: all 878 import relationships in scan-result.json's importMap already have a corresponding 'imports' edge in the assembled graph (file-to-file, verified 1:1) -- no cross-batch edges needed to be added.
Final graph: 1275 nodes (+3), 2401 edges (+18), zero dangling edges, zero duplicate (source,target,type) keys, zero duplicate node IDs.

Remaining known gap (intentionally left as-is): ~30 dangling references to simple exported constants (contract-constants.ts, assistant prompts.ts/settings.ts, types/database.ts helpers) were not modeled as nodes by their batches; recreating placeholder nodes for every such constant was judged to add noise without architectural value, consistent with the merge script's own note that this class of drop is expected.
